1391.1: Swayye in praise of the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Blessed is that all-pervading Being, the Maker, the Cause, the Creator who fashions creation, the all-powerful. Blessed is the True Guru Nanak, who set his hand upon your forehead (O Guru Angad). Then he placed his hand on (your) forehead, and of itself the Amrit poured down in torrents; gods, men, ganas and sages were openly steeped in its fragrance. Roaring, you slew Death, the thorn; you held back the wandering (mind); you gathered up the five demons (the passions) and kept them in one house. At the Guru's door you have conquered the world; you play the game of even-mindedness; keeping your attention on the Formless One, you hold the chariot (of the mind) in the state of unman. O Kalsahar, tell through the seven continents the glory of Lahna, who has touched the Guru of the world (Guru Nanak), (one with) Murari. ॥1॥

Ganas: the attendants of Shiva. The seven continents (dips): the earth as the Puranas divide it, the whole world. Unman: the state of the mind raised above the world's thoughts and settled in the Lord. Lahna is Guru Angad Dev Ji's name before he became Guru.
1391.2: He whose glance is a stream of Amrit, that digs out the stain (of sin) and lifts it away; the sight of whose door drives off the darkness of ignorance; those who serve the sublime Shabad, a hard and arduous task, he has carried across the world-ocean and set free of their load; in the Sat Sangat they take hold of Sahaj; through the Guru's teaching they awake; humble, they live ever in supreme love. O Kalsahar, tell through the seven continents the glory of Lahna, who has touched the Guru of the world (Guru Nanak), (one with) Murari. ॥2॥
1391.3: You have made the infinite Name firm (in your heart); your spotless glory is spread wide; you are the support of the life of seekers, Siddhas and the good. You are King Janak come again; (your) Shabad is sublime in the world; you live in the world as the lotus lives in water. You are the wish-fulfilling tree, the healer of ills, the remover of the world's fevers; souls of the three kinds hold their attention on you in one unbroken strain. O Kalsahar, tell through the seven continents the glory of Lahna, who has touched the Guru of the world (Guru Nanak), (one with) Murari. ॥3॥
The wish-fulfilling tree (kalap taru): the tree of heaven in the Puranas that grants every wish. Souls of the three kinds: all beings, living in Maya's three qualities (rajas, tamas and sattva).
1391.4: You have received honour from the revered Presence (Guru Nanak); you served the approved Guru, who subdued the python (of the mind) and raised it high; whose sight is as the sight of the Lord, Har Har, whose soul is rich in wisdom: the state of that approved Guru, (one with) the undivided Lord, you have come to know; his gaze rests on the unmoving place, his pure understanding stays in the highest place; wearing the armour of gentleness, he has broken the power (of Maya). O Kalsahar, tell through the seven continents the glory of Lahna, who has touched the Guru of the world (Guru Nanak), (one with) Murari. ॥4॥
1391.5: (O Guru Angad,) casting your glance, you take away darkness, burn up wrongs and destroy sins; you are the mighty hero of the Shabad, the destroyer of lust and anger; you bring greed and attachment under control, and cherish the beggars who come to your refuge; you have gathered in the love of the spirit, and your words pour out fair streams of Amrit. O Kal, the True Guru is the crowning mark of the True Gurus; whoever clings to him in faith crosses over. The Guru of the world, Pheru's lion of a son, Angad: Lahna exercises Raj and Jog. ॥5॥
Baba Pheru was Guru Angad Dev Ji's father.
1392.1: His attention stays ever on the undivided (Lord); in what he does he is free, moving at his own will. Like a tree laden with fruit he bows down and bears hardship; pure is his thought. He has known this essence: the unknowable, wondrous (Lord) pervades all. With natural ease he has watered (hearts) by the ray of his fair bani, full of Amrit. (O Guru Angad,) you have reached the rank the Guru (Nanak) attained, and taken up truth and contentment. Kal proclaims aloud: those who have had the sight of Lahna have touched the Lord. ॥6॥
1392.2: You have found faith in your mind; the revered Presence (Guru Nanak) has given you access to the Profound (Lord). The deadly poison has fled from your body; you have drunk the Amrit deep within. In your heart the light has dawned (of him), the Unknowable, who has set his power through the ages. The True Guru, in the samadhi (deep meditative absorption) of Sahaj, is absorbed (in the Lord), who pervades all alike, without a break. He is large-hearted, the remover of poverty; at the sight of him sins take fright. Kal says: ever in love, in Sahaj, I utter the praise of Lahna with my tongue. ॥7॥
1392.3: The Name is the medicine, the Name the support, and the Name the peace of samadhi; the banner of the Name ever shines (over him). O Kal, he is dyed deep in love through the Name; the Name makes gods and men fragrant. Whoever has gained the touch of the Name (from him), the sun of his truth has risen over the world. Beholding the Guru, the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage is done. ॥8॥
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: the tiraths held most holy in India.
1392.4: The True (Name) is his place of pilgrimage, the True his bathing, and love for the True his food; ever speaking the True, he shines. He has found the True through the Guru's Shabad; the True Name makes the Sangats fragrant. He whose self-restraint is the True, whose fast is the True: O humble poet Kal, tell (of him): Beholding the Guru, the True (Name) is found, and one's birth is approved. ॥9॥
1392.5: He casts his auspicious glance, full of Amrit, and takes away wrongs, sins and all filth; lust, anger, greed and attachment, and pride, all of them he brings under control. Peace dwells ever in (his) mind; he takes away the sorrow of the world. The Guru is a river of the nine treasures; he washes away the stain of our births. O Tal, say: that Guru should be served day and night, in Sahaj and with love. Beholding the Guru, the pain of birth and death departs. ॥10॥
Tal: another name the Bhatt Kal uses for himself.
